facts.label: Already e yet em reservas
facts.sub: Já: have already + particípio. Ainda não: haven’t + particípio + yet. Pergunta: Have you booked yet?

facts.label: Já
facts.sub: Use already para dizer que algo foi feito. Ele fica entre have e o particípio: I have already paid the deposit. Mostra que a ação terminou antes do que alguém esperava ou perguntou.

facts.label: Ainda
facts.sub: Use yet em perguntas e frases negativas. Ele fica no fim: Have you booked yet? I haven’t booked yet. Não use yet em frases afirmativas comuns sobre algo já feito.

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: Already means something is done before now.
Yet goes in affirmative sentences about the past.
items.why: Yet is for questions and negatives.

items.s: “I have just paid” means a moment ago.

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.
group: Cada aluno decide sozinho, depois compare as respostas e peça uma justificativa.
Corrija pela pista do texto, não só dizendo “certo/errado”.
extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: Already means something is done before now. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)
Yet goes in affirmative sentences about the past. → Falso (Yet is for questions and negatives.)
“I have just paid” means a moment ago. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)

paragraphs: It is a cold Saturday morning in London. Emma and Nina are planning a short trip for spring. Emma has already found a hotel online. Nina has looked at some pages, but she has not chosen one yet. They sit in the lobby of a small hotel to ask questions. A friendly receptionist waits behind the desk.

“Nina, have you booked a hotel room in London yet?” says Emma. “Not yet. I have already looked at three hotels, but I haven’t decided.” says Nina. “I have already made a reservation at a small hotel near the station.” says Emma.
